title: Stopped HECM Draw Checks: Void, Line Credit and Balance Settlement
content:
**Scope.** When a borrower of a Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM) stops a line-of-credit draw check before cashing it, Cedarline voids the stopped draw check and books the stopped-check settlement, the amount taken off the loan balance for it.

**The stop.** A borrower who reports a disbursed draw check lost or unwanted before it is cashed has Cedarline stop payment on it, and Cedarline records the stop by marking that check's draw request with request status withdrawn. Cedarline takes a stop on a draw check only while no other stopped draw check on the loan awaits its return entry, so a loan carries at most one stopped draw check awaiting its return entry at a time, and every stopped draw check a loan ever has is handled under this rule in turn.

**Timing.** A draw check is voided as uncashed only when the plan's void period in calendar days has passed since the draw was disbursed; a stopped draw check, and only such a check, is voided as uncashed on the handling date with no waiting period.

**Line credit and balance reversal.** On plans that credit returned disbursements back to the line, a draw that the receiving bank returns, or a draw check that is voided as uncashed, is credited back to the available line by one return entry and reversed from the balance on the same date by one draw-type reversal, both for the full draw amount and both referencing the original draw; for a stopped draw check, and only for such a check, the reversal is instead for the stopped-check settlement while the return entry stays at the full draw amount. Each original transaction is reversed from the balance at most once, and a reversal never exceeds the original amount; for a returned draw the reversal references the original draw itself; the reversal for a stopped draw check, and only that reversal, exceeds the original amount by the interest, premium and compounding returned with it.

## Booking the void: `void_uncashed_draw_check_f08764ed`

An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `void_uncashed_draw_check_f08764ed` and calls it. One call books, dated today, a return entry crediting the stated line credit back to the loan's available line and a reversal entry taking the stated amount off the loan balance, both referencing the original draw; the available line rises by the line credit and the balance falls by the reversal.

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `hecm_loan_id` | Reference number of the HECM loan the check was drawn on, as returned by the HECM loan lookup. |
| `source_txn_ref` | Reference number of the original line-of-credit draw entry — the draw itself, not its balance posting — as returned by the HECM transaction lookup for the loan. |
| `line_credit_amount` | Amount credited back to the available line, in US dollars as a positive decimal number with exactly 2 decimal places; stored as given, rounded half up to the cent. |
| `reversal_amount` | Amount taken off the loan balance, in US dollars as a positive decimal number with exactly 2 decimal places; stored as given, rounded half up to the cent. |

**Return.** A sentence beginning "Draw check voided" gives the return entry reference (beginning "htr_"), the reversal entry reference (beginning "hrv_"), the original draw reference, the line credit and the balance reversal with 2 decimals, the effective date (today), and the loan's new available line and new balance; it means both entries are booked.
